newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end up sharply on wheat, technicals.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end up sharply on wheat, technicals.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed sharply higher on the back of a rally in wheat, with fund buying and bull spreading pushing the soy complex into a technical breakout, traders said.

"Everyone wanted to be easier this morning after yesterday's close but wheat took over plus the oats bullish consensus was down to 22 which was very oversold," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co. "Oats and wheat caught everyone in the corn and bean pits on the short side."
Soybeans rallied Monday, dropped Tuesday but sprang back convincingly Wednesday as the market prepared for export news.
USDA at 0730 CST Thursday will release its updated weekly export sales report and sales of U.S. soybeans and soy products have been occurring at a rapid clip featuring China as a buyer.
Trader expectations were for the net export sales tally for soybeans in Thursday's USDA report to range from 500,000 to 700,000 tonnes.
Soybeans closed seven to 11-1/2 cents higher, with January up 11-1/2 at $7.07 per bushel.
Soybeans sagged early but came roaring back when wheat continued to march higher.
Traders said the rally Monday was pounced on by shorts Tuesday as cash soybean markets reached $7.00 per bushel in some locations.
"The basis in some areas got farmers $7.00 beans and there was some selling," a trader said.

The weakness in the November during Tuesday's expiration also captured attention. "There were 1.25 million bushels still open in the November (early Wednesday) so someone is going to deliver," the trader said.
Technicians awoke to what some said was a key breakout amid an outside day up.
"It was an outside day up and good. It was higher than yesterday's high and lower than yesterday's low and it closed higher which could mean a key move to the upside," a floor technician said.
"But it has to be followed by two more days up. On a technicial basis this was a big indicator," he said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 48,000 contracts, above the 41,153 traded Tuesday, according to the CBOT.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 12,000 contracts, above the 11,146 traded Tuesday.
